Growing that fast and thriving comes down to our people. Our team is our biggest asset and one that we’re proud of. We’re committed to maintaining our vibrant culture as we continue to grow.

About the role

Aquablu's products run Android in more places than your pocket. Our dispensing systems ship with Android-powered on-device software that hundreds of thousands of people touch every day, and our mobile apps put hydration in users' hands. As our Android Engineer, you work across that whole surface.

Your main arena is on-device: the software running on the hardware itself, where Android meets the physical world. Screens people tap on a machine, software that talks to firmware, updates that roll out to hundreds of deployed systems in the field. Alongside that, you contribute to our mobile development where the products need it. Few Android roles give you this range.

This is a hands-on engineering role in a small, fast team. You own features end to end and deliver them reliably, reaching out to your manager when support is needed to unblock you. You build with AI agents as your default collaborator, you work cross-functionally with hardware, firmware, and product, proactively identifying and reaching out to key players that can help filling any gaps.

This role reports into our Head of Digital Product, and is part of Aquablu’s Software & Intelligence Engineering team.


What You'll Build & Own

  • On-device Android software: Features on the user-facing software running on our dispensing systems — UI, device behaviour, and the integration layer where software meets hardware. You own your features end to end.

  • Fleet-ready releases: Contribute to releases that update reliably across hundreds of deployed devices in the field, where a broken release means a technician visit. The riskiest releases get a second pair of senior eyes — and you learn what makes them safe.

  • Hardware & firmware integration: Work with embedded and firmware engineers to define and implement serial APIs (UART), that expose device state and trigger mechanical actions.

  • Mobile contribution: Support Android development on our consumer app where the roadmap needs it.

  • AI-native development: Build with AI agents every day and keep pushing what that lets you ship.

What You Bring

You should be able to judge which Android patterns fit a non-standard system, and to design features that contribute to a scalable, reliable system.

  • Curiosity for Android beyond the traditional mobile world: kiosk, embedded, or AOSP work is a strong plus. Pragmatic problem solver who’s comfortable working outside of familiar mobile patterns.

jobs.title: Cross-Functional Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.


We want you as a Cross-Functional Mechanical Engineer to bring hands-on structural design experience and sound engineering judgement to the mechanical development and verification of Nyx. With a strong system-level mindset, you will support subsystem teams in developing robust designs, resolving mechanical challenges, and substantiating the integrity of critical hardware throughout the development lifecycle.

A key focus of your role will be to develop and consolidate the mechanical justifications supporting NASA requirements compliance and Safety Review Panel (SRP) activities. Working with subsystem owners and the safety and certification teams, you will establish the technical basis for allowable damage and failure criteria across critical vehicle components. You will combine direct technical contributions with practical guidance to engineers and suppliers, connecting component-level assessments with vehicle-level requirements and safety considerations.

You will be part of the Nyx Design Office Team, within the Cross-Functional Mechanical team, and will report to the Integrated Mechanical Sizing & Assurance Team Leader.


Key Responsibilities:

Technical Leadership & Integration

  • Provide hands-on structural design expertise and technical guidance across subsystems, supporting mechanical integrity and consistency at vehicle level.

  • Assess load paths, interfaces, stiffness, and boundary conditions to understand how mechanical, pressure, and thermo-mechanical loads are transferred through components, attachments, and the vehicle structure.

  • Perform and review mechanical assessments using engineering calculations, finite element analysis (FEA), and test evidence, challenging assumptions and identifying the failure modes that drive design decisions.

  • Support subsystem owners in translating high-level mechanical requirements into subsystem and component specifications, maintaining traceability and accounting for vehicle-level interactions.

Compliance & Verification

  • Develop and document mechanical justifications for allowable damage and failure criteria for critical Nyx hardware, in collaboration with the relevant subsystem and discipline specialists.

  • Establish the supporting rationale through analysis and test evidence, addressing relevant strength, stability, fatigue, fracture, damage tolerance, and residual performance considerations as applicable to each component.

  • Support NASA SRP activities by preparing mechanical justification, contributing to compliance matrices and verification evidence, and addressing technical questions and review actions with the safety and certification teams.

  • Review qualification strategies, test plans, and reports for consistency with applicable NASA requirements, agreed standards, and the assumptions used in mechanical analyses.

  • Participate in design reviews, identify gaps in mechanical justification, and recommend design changes or additional verification activities to resolve them.

Supplier Interactions and Team Collaboration

  • Review supplier designs, structural analyses, and verification documentation to assess technical maturity and consistency with subsystem and vehicle requirements at key milestones.

  • Provide practical technical guidance to suppliers and subsystem owners, resolving mechanical issues and following technical actions through to closure.

  • Facilitate technical alignment between subsystem teams, structural analysis, materials and processes, testing, safety and certification, and suppliers, ensuring that assumptions, interfaces, and responsibilities are clearly understood.

What We Would Love to See from You

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent relevant practical experience.

  • Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience in mechanical or structural engineering within the aerospace or aeronautics industry.

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience designing and justifying structural or mechanical hardware through development and qualification, in aerospace or aeronautics.

  • Experience assessing relevant failure mechanisms and developing defensible mechanical justifications, including damage acceptance or failure criteria for safety-critical hardware.

  • Ability to perform and critically review engineering calculations and FEA, interpret CAD models and engineering drawings, and relate analysis assumptions to the physical design and test configuration.

  • Understanding of mechanical requirements flow-down, qualification and verification processes, and traceable compliance evidence, together with familiarity with applicable space standards and NASA requirements.

  • Demonstrated ability to guide engineers and suppliers through complex mechanical problems while considering subsystem interfaces and vehicle-level consequences.

Additional experience we would value:

  • Direct involvement in NASA safety reviews or SRP submissions, particularly the preparation and defence of mechanical qualification and the closure of review actions.

  • Experience with pressurized structures, fluid piping, radiators, or propulsion hardware, and with fracture control, damage tolerance, or structural test campaigns.

Skills and Behaviors:

  • System-Level Thinking: Ability to connect component-level design and failure mechanisms with subsystem interfaces, vehicle performance, and safety objectives.

  • Engineering Judgement: Ability to identify governing load paths and failure modes, challenge modelling assumptions, and distinguish between a numerical result and a sound mechanical justification.

  • Influence & Decision-Making: Ability to guide technical decisions across teams and suppliers through clear reasoning and evidence, while working within agreed technical responsibilities.

  • Mentorship: Ability to share practical design experience and help engineers strengthen their structural understanding and verification practices.

  • Stakeholder Management: Ability to work constructively with internal teams, suppliers, and external reviewers, including NASA, in coordination with the safety and certification teams.

  • Problem-Solving: Proactive in identifying mechanical risks, prioritizing substantiation gaps, and developing proportionate solutions that protect technical integrity and program objectives.

  • Communication: Clear and structured communicator, able to explain assumptions, load paths, failure criteria, and supporting evidence to different technical audiences.

  • Demonstrates behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Vision, Competence, Integrity and Passion.

  • Fluent in English. Knowledge of German, French and Italian is an asset.

Your profile

Collaboration is fundamental to achieving our ambition. We nurture genuine relationships with global partners in our drive to make SAF the alternative to fossil jet fuel.

Our in-house team of SAF experts have helped over 60 airlines and corporates reduce their climate impact using the Book & Claim mechanism; the most transparent and traceable way to support aviation sustainability with real emission reductions.

About the Role

Every month, hundreds of potential customers show interest in Trengo. They start a free trial, request a demo, or leave their contact details. But not everyone gets the personal follow-up they need to take the next step.

That's where you come in.

As our Marketing Development Representative (MDR), you'll be the first personal point of contact for potential customers, helping them find the right way to get started with Trengo.

You'll join our Growth Marketing team and work closely with Sales, sitting right at the intersection of marketing and sales. You'll turn the demand we generate into real business opportunities, whether that's booking a meeting with an Account Executive or helping someone become a paying customer through our self-serve journey.

This is a hands-on junior role where you'll get to learn how a fast-moving AI SaaS company turns marketing efforts into revenue, with plenty of room to experiment, develop your skills, and make a measurable impact.

It's an 8-month contract with the possibility of extension.

About Trengo

Welcome to the forefront of AI-driven communication. At Trengo, we’re redefining the industry by replacing repetitive work with meaningful conversations through our AI-powered customer engagement platform. We unify communication channels and leverage agentic AI to deliver proactive, human-like service, boosting efficiency for thousands of businesses worldwide.

As a fast-moving Dutch scale-up, backed by a $36M Series A and an official WhatsApp Business Solutions Provider, we thrive on acceleration. Your expertise will drive growth: you’ll make a strategic impact, champion AI innovation, and help shape the product roadmap. You’ll do this alongside an international team guided by our Dynamic pace, Future-proof mindset, Ownership, and Open culture.

What your role looks like:

Turn inbound interest into opportunities

  • Be the first personal point of contact for new inbound leads, reaching out through calls and personalised emails, ideally within the same working day.

  • Follow up with qualified free-trial sign-ups, demo requests and prospects who have expressed interest but haven't booked a meeting.

  • Re-engage prospects whose meetings weren't booked, were cancelled or resulted in a no-show, and help them take the next step.

  • Connect qualified prospects with the right Account Executive, making sure they have the context needed for a productive conversation.

Help prospects become self-serve customers

  • Reach out to prospects who might not be the right fit for a sales conversation but could still benefit from Trengo.

  • Understand what they're looking for, answer initial questions and guide them towards the right self-serve plan.

  • Follow up with free-trial users to help them get started and encourage them to take the next step towards becoming customers.

Improve how we engage with leads

  • Experiment with different outreach messages, sequences and follow-up approaches to understand what converts best.

  • Share insights with Marketing and Sales about common objections, lead quality and what prospects are looking for.

  • Keep HubSpot accurate and up to date by logging interactions, tracking outcomes and maintaining clean lead data.

How we'll measure success

You'll have a direct impact on our growth, with clear results you can track:

  • Speed of follow-up: Making sure inbound prospects receive timely, personal attention.

  • Meetings generated: Booking qualified meetings that turn into conversations with our Account Executives.

  • Self-serve conversions: Helping prospects progress from initial interest to becoming paying customers.

  • Continuous improvement: Finding better ways to engage prospects and sharing insights that help our Marketing and Sales teams improve.

The tools you'll work with

You'll get hands-on experience with our commercial and AI toolkit:

  • HubSpot: CRM, lead management, outreach sequences and calling.

  • RevenueHero: Lead routing and meeting booking.

  • Fathom: Call recordings, feedback and coaching.

  • Slack & Notion: Team collaboration, processes and playbooks.

  • AI tools: Researching prospects, personalising outreach and experimenting with smarter ways of working.

What you’ll bring

  • 1-2 years of experience, ideally through an internship or an early-career role in sales, marketing, customer success or a customer-facing environment.

  • Fluent English, both written and spoken. Dutch is a big plus.

  • Confidence in communication: You're comfortable picking up the phone, writing personalised emails and starting conversations with people you haven't met.

  • A proactive mindset: You don't wait for someone to tell you what to do next. You spot opportunities and take initiative.

  • An organised way of working: You can manage multiple conversations, prioritise your day and follow through on commitments.

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn: You're interested in SaaS, AI and how businesses grow, and you're open to coaching and feedback.

  • A results-driven attitude: You enjoy working towards clear goals, experimenting with different approaches and understanding what works.

Nice to have

  • Experience working with HubSpot or other CRM tools.

  • Exposure to inbound lead follow-up, prospecting or sales processes.

  • Additional language skills such as Dutch, German, French, Spanish or Italian.

  • Familiarity with eCommerce, WhatsApp Business or customer communication platforms.

  • Experience using AI tools to research prospects, personalise communication or improve workflows.

⚙️ Our tech & AI mindset

AI is not a buzzword at Trengo — it’s part of how we build and operate. You’ll work with AI-driven features, automation, data, or tools that help us move faster and smarter. We value thoughtful use of AI that creates real value for customers and teams.

What’s in it for you?

This is what we carefully prepared for you:

  • 🚀 A key role where you’ll make a visible impact in a vibrant scale-up environment.

  • 🌍 Hybrid working + 2 months per year to work abroad.

  • 🏗️ A strong onboarding program with hands-on training and a dedicated buddy to set you up for success.

  • 🧘 Mental health support with free sessions from on-demand psychologists (OpenUp).

  • 📚 Learning budget + 2 extra days off to attend courses or conferences.

  • 🌴 28 vacation days to rest, recharge, and travel

  • 🚆 Travel reimbursement to our Utrecht HQ.

  • 📶 Monthly internet & phone allowance to stay connected.

  • 🗣️ Dutch courses for our international colleagues.

  • 🍴 Daily warm lunches prepared by our workplace experience team when you’re at our beautiful Utrecht office.

  • 💼 Pension contribution to help you plan for the future.

  • 🛫 Sabbatical: After two years, enjoy up to three months away (unpaid) to rest, recharge, or see the world.

🔍 Our hiring process

  1. Introductory call – First conversation with our Talent team.

  2. Manager interview – Deep dive into experience and expectations.

  3. Practical assignment – Role-related, real-world challenge.

  4. Team connection – Meet future colleagues and confirm mutual fit.

We aim to keep the process clear, fair, and timely, and we’ll keep you informed at every step.

Your next challenge starts here!

Join us in building the future of customer engagement — we’d love to have you on the team.

👉 Apply today and let’s grow together!

jobs.title: Senior SEO & GEO Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are

We believe travel can create Citizens of the World. When people cross Europe slowly, by train, they come back more curious, more open and better able to understand people unlike themselves.

 

With colleagues from more than 50 countries, our diversity sparks curiosity, insight and a culture of openness, which is essential to understanding our travellers and one another.

 

Three values connect everyone at Interrail: we lead with our purpose, we own our impact, and we choose for growth.

 

We work in a hybrid way, from our office in Utrecht and our homes across the Netherlands.

 

Who we’re looking for

Someone who can shape how travellers discover Interrail, whether they’re typing into a search engine or asking an AI assistant to plan their trip. Exploring Europe by rail is one of the most transformative ways to travel, and there’s a big, untapped opportunity to make it even easier. With SEO and GEO, you’ll help travellers get inspired, plan and book their next rail adventure with an Interrail Pass in fewer steps.

 

Also, it’s good to know that the team has agreed to meet in the office every Tuesday and Thursday, so you’ll be expected to be in the office on these days to work side by side with your colleagues.

 

What you’ll be doing

You’ll be joining the Growth team (in a nutshell: the people who turn traveller curiosity into journeys booked), reporting to our E-Commerce Lead.

 

You’ll own the end-to-end SEO and GEO strategy, so that Interrail is found, cited and recommended wherever travellers research rail travel in Europe. Working across content, product, engineering and PR/brand, you’ll turn search and AI visibility insight into meaningful, measurable growth.

 

Strategy and leadership

  • Own and scale a unified SEO and GEO strategy and roadmap, aligned to commercial goals across our priority markets.

  • Prioritise investment across markets and languages based on search demand, commercial opportunity and local traveller needs.

  • Be our internal expert on how AI is changing travel discovery, embedding SEO and GEO thinking across marketing, content, PR/brand and product.

  • Partner with engineering, content and product to get the right work prioritised and shipped.

Technical SEO and architecture

  • Own technical SEO for our large, complex site and set the technical roadmap with product and content.

  • Lead our SEO architecture: hreflang at scale, domain and subfolder strategy, and localisation quality across languages.

  • Make sure search engines and AI systems can access and understand the site, with the right structured data and clear, consistent information on passes, pricing and eligibility.

  • Own our crawler access policy for AI bots together with legal and engineering, balancing visibility against content protection.

GEO

  • Own our GEO strategy and roadmap: how we earn mentions, citations and recommendations across markets and languages.

  • Build our GEO measurement framework, tracking brand presence, citation share, share of voice against competitors and sentiment.

  • Spot recurring inaccuracies in AI-generated answers, fix them at the source with the relevant teams and track whether accuracy improves.

  • Partner with PR, partnerships and social to strengthen the off-site signals AI models rely on, from trusted travel publications to community presence and review platforms.

  • Measure and attribute AI-referred traffic and conversions, and run structured tests to build repeatable GEO playbooks.

  • Assess emerging opportunities, such as AI agents that plan and book travel, and advise on what Interrail needs to be ready.

Content and topical authority

  • Shape content strategy and topical authority across destinations, routes, guides and inspiration, balancing discovery with pass and booking intent.

  • Make sure our content performs in both search results and AI answers, with clear factual structure and original rail expertise worth citing.

  • Be the SEO and GEO advisor to the content team, building a shared roadmap that connects visibility opportunity to editorial output.

  • Set and govern content quality standards (briefs, structure, internal linking, E-E-A-T) and upskill the team in SEO and GEO best practice.

  • Identify gaps, cannibalisation and refresh opportunities, and advise on what to create, update, consolidate or retire.

Measurement and reporting

  • Forecast organic and AI-driven performance, set KPIs across both, and report clearly to senior stakeholders.

What success looks like

  • Non-brand searches make up a growing share of organic traffic and revenue across our priority markets.

  • A GEO measurement framework is live, and our citation share and share of voice in AI answers are improving against key competitors.

  • The SEO and GEO roadmap is agreed with product, engineering and content and delivered as planned, including website and CMS changes that launch without loss of organic visibility.

  • Recurring inaccuracies about passes, pricing and eligibility in AI answers are identified, fixed at the source and measurably reduced.

What we’re looking for

Here’s what will help you in this role. If you don’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you.

 

In terms of your experience and skills:

  • Demonstrated experience leading SEO strategy across content and technical, ideally in travel, e-commerce or a large content or marketplace environment.

  • Hands-on GEO experience, with examples of your approach, results, measurement limitations and the decisions that followed.

  • A working understanding of how AI search experiences select and cite sources, and how that differs from traditional ranking.

  • A strong track record in international and multilingual SEO at scale.

  • A solid technical foundation, including structured data, and the ability to influence engineering roadmaps.

  • Outstanding cross-functional collaboration: you align teams around a shared roadmap and take initiatives from idea to launch without direct authority, reviewing results together and applying the learnings.

  • A data-driven, commercial mindset: comfortable forecasting, sizing opportunity, attributing impact in a maturing channel and presenting to leadership.

  • A test-and-learn mindset, comfortable building new capabilities in a fast-changing environment.

  • Experience partnering closely with content, editorial, PR or brand teams.

  • Fluency with the core toolset: Google Search Console, GA4, an SEO platform such as Semrush or Ahrefs, a crawler such as Screaming Frog, log-analysis tools and GEO tracking tools.

  • Fluent English; another European language, ideally German, French, Italian or Spanish, is beneficial to have.

Our offer

  • A hybrid way of working, with some days each week in our Utrecht office and the rest from home.

  • A free NS train card, so you can travel across the Netherlands for work and in your free time.

  • A free Interrail Pass every year for you and a companion, so you can travel across Europe the way our travellers do.

  • Unlimited access to OpenUp, an online wellbeing platform.

  • A personal wellbeing allowance of up to €1,500.

  • A training allowance of up to €4,000 for learning that’s relevant to your role.

  • A variable annual bonus (target 4%), based on company and individual performance.

  • An annual team trip across Europe, so you see first-hand what our travellers experience.

  • The option to work from abroad for 20 days a year.

  • An annual leave package of 28 days, plus study days, volunteer days and a culture day.

  • Salary Scale: 60. Monthly gross salary (excluding 8% holiday allowance): €5,300 – €6,400 (full-time), based on experience.

Curious to apply?

Apply directly through our careers page.

 

  • We’ll ask you to share your CV in English (our business language) and tell us why you’re interested in Interrail and this role. It doesn’t hurt to be creative; we enjoy seeing your personality shine through.

  • For some roles, we may also ask you to complete a short task based on the real job, so you can show us your skills in practice.

 

If we’d like to get to know you better, the next step is a first conversation with Talent Acquisition, followed by interviews with the team. It’s a two-way conversation: a chance for you to explore Interrail, and for us to get to know you.

 

To keep our hiring fair, we use blind screening in the early stages. Your name, photo, date of birth, gender, nationality, contact details and social media links are hidden, so our first decisions are based only on your skills, experience and potential.

 

In the meantime

If you’re curious, why not check us out on LinkedIn and get a sense of our culture and values?

 

Got questions? Our team would be happy to help: just drop us a note at

 

While you’re here, you can plan your own trip and find your Pass at www.interrail.com.

jobs.title: Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
Position Overview

Axelera AI is a fast-growing AI semiconductor company headquartered in Eindhoven, building high-performance, energy-efficient AI acceleration hardware and software, from the Metis AI platform for edge inference to next-generation AI processing units. We are scaling quickly: new customers, new partners, new markets, and a growing volume of complex commercial deals across the global semiconductor supply chain.

We are looking for an experienced commercial lawyer to be the engine of our commercial legal function. You will close deals, build the playbooks and processes that let the business move fast without taking on unmanaged risk, and lead how legal operates day to day, with AI in the loop so a lean team delivers more with less. This is a hands-on role with real scope to shape the function as it grows.

Key responsibilities:

Commercial contracting

  • Draft, review and negotiate a high volume of commercial agreements: customer, distribution, reseller and OEM/ODM agreements; sales terms and EULAs; supply and manufacturing agreements (foundry, OSAT, component suppliers); technology and IP licences; software and SaaS agreements; evaluation, early access and development agreements; R&D collaboration and consortium agreements; services and vendor agreements; and MOUs, LOIs and partnership terms.

  • Act as the trusted, pragmatic adviser to Sales, Product, Engineering, Operations and Finance, giving clear, commercial risk calls at pace.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

The Opportunity

Prosus is continuing to evolve its business, product and investment activities, with ambitious plans to build, scale and grow technology-driven businesses and products globally.

We are looking for a highly organised, proactive and resourceful Executive Assistant to provide high-quality executive and operational support to three senior leaders: the Chief Product Officer, the Head of Ventures, and the Director of Strategy & Operations. You will play an important part in enabling these leaders to operate effectively, ensuring their time and priorities are managed efficiently and that the day-to-day running of their respective areas is seamless.

You will take ownership of complex calendars, international travel, meeting preparation, stakeholder coordination and administrative processes, while anticipating needs, managing competing priorities and identifying opportunities to improve how things are done. Working across different teams and functions, you will build strong relationships throughout the organisation and act as a trusted point of contact for both internal and external stakeholders.

We are looking for someone who combines exceptional organisational skills with sound judgement, discretion and a hands-on approach. Someone who enjoys being one step ahead, takes pride in making things happen and thrives in an environment where priorities can move quickly.

What You Will Do

  • Manage expenses, invoices, budget tracking and other administrative processes, ensuring accuracy and compliance with company policies.

  • Handle confidential and sensitive information with the highest level of discretion and professionalism.

Stakeholder & Operational Coordination

  • Support the coordination of cross-functional initiatives, helping ensure meetings, communications and follow-up actions are organised and delivered effectively.

  • Assist with onboarding and administrative arrangements for new team members and other relevant stakeholders across the supported functions.

  • Coordinate with HR, Finance, IT, Workplace, Legal and other internal teams to resolve requests and ensure efficient day-to-day operations.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify administrative processes, improve ways of working and create greater efficiency for the executives and their teams.

  • Provide general operational support across the three functions, stepping in where needed to keep priorities moving and ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

Who You Are

You are a highly organised, proactive and solutions-oriented professional who enjoys working closely with senior leaders and making their lives easier.

You naturally think several steps ahead, have a strong sense of ownership and are comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment. You know when to take initiative, when to escalate and how to exercise sound judgement without needing constant direction.

You are confident in engaging with senior stakeholders, build relationships easily and communicate clearly and professionally. You are equally comfortable managing the finer details of a complex travel itinerary as you are coordinating a senior leadership meeting or resolving an unexpected scheduling challenge.

Above all, you are dependable, discreet and take pride in delivering excellent support. You enjoy being behind the scenes, making things happen and creating the conditions for others to perform at their best.

What You Bring

  • Proven experience in an Executive Assistant, Senior Personal Assistant or Executive Business Partner role, ideally supporting multiple senior executives.

  • Experience working in a fast-paced, international and complex business environment, preferably within technology, investment or a corporate organisation.

  • Exceptional organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex calendars and competing priorities.

  • Strong experience coordinating international travel, meetings, leadership events and other executive-level logistics.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to interact professionally with senior stakeholders and external partners.

  • A proactive, hands-on mindset, with the ability to anticipate needs, solve problems independently and take ownership of tasks from start to finish.

  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy while working at pace.

  • High levels of discretion, integrity and professionalism when handling confidential and sensitive information.

  • Comfortable working across different teams and functions, building relationships and navigating a complex organisational environment.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other relevant productivity and collaboration tools.

  • Fluent in English, both written and spoken.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

📊 About our Data Quality & Provenance Team

Our Data Quality & Provenance team sits within Wayve’s AI Platform organisation and builds the evidence that helps teams make confident decisions about the data underpinning our embodied AI systems. We develop statistically robust methods, metrics and tools to determine when data-quality, annotation and evaluation signals can be trusted—and when they cannot.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Define measurable, statistically rigorous concepts of data quality, including coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

  • Apply statistical-inference methods to multi-rater annotation, label ambiguity, dataset coverage and black-box model evaluation.

  • Partner with annotation, autonomy and evaluation teams to translate practical quality questions into defensible metrics.

  • Build automated reports that clearly communicate confidence, limitations and appropriate interpretation.

  • Analyse large annotation datasets using Python and SQL to identify quality issues and inform decisions.

  • Iterate on metrics and reporting based on feedback from the teams using them.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Statistical methods for distinguishing genuine data-quality problems from label ambiguity, inconsistent annotation or evaluation noise.

  • Labeler and dataset metrics that support training-data selection, simulation, annotation acceptance and model evaluation.

  • Reusable quality artefacts that replace one-off analyses with registered, automated metrics and reports.

  • Multi-rater and human-in-the-loop ML systems, including approaches such as Dawid–Skene-style models, psychometrics and inter-rater agreement.

  • Quality standards spanning coverage, uncertainty, provenance, annotation quality and predictive-model performance.

  • Integration of data-science outputs into the platform workflows used by engineering and research teams

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have strong foundations in classical statistics, including experimental design, sampling, modelling, estimation and inference.

  • You have practical experience with rater or annotator modelling, inter-rater agreement, label uncertainty or related methods.

  • You understand data quality across dimensions such as coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

  • You have worked with annotation tooling, QA methodologies, human-in-the-loop ML systems or multi-rater labelled datasets.

  • You have strong Python and SQL skills and are confident analysing large, complex datasets.

  • You can turn ambiguous stakeholder questions into rigorous, usable metrics and clearly communicate uncertainty, limitations and decision implications.

  • Experience with probabilistic or Bayesian modelling, production platform integrations or safety-critical data would be an advantage.


🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency interview: Python Programming (60 mins) Data Curation Domain (60 mins)

  • Deep-dive interview: Hiring Manager Interview (60 mins) Systems design interview (60 mins)

  • Final interview: Mission and values alignment (45 mins)

    We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

jobs.title: Technical Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales (UK)
jobs.description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

You'll be the deepest technical voice in our sales cycle — the person who can sit with an engineering team, read their stack, and build a working Dust integration before the meeting is over. This role goes well beyond demos: you'll write code, design integration architectures, navigate enterprise security and compliance reviews, and own technically complex POCs with large enterprise and engineering-led accounts. You'll also help shape the SE function itself — building internal tooling and playbooks, mentoring more junior SEs, and feeding direct technical insight into our product roadmap.

 

What you'll do

Lead Engineering-Level Technical Evaluations

  • Partner with Account Executives as the primary technical voice for enterprise and engineering-led accounts — the person who earns trust in a room full of engineers and DSIs

  • Run architecture deep-dives, API walkthroughs, and live integration builds with customer engineering teams — not just polished slides

  • Own the technical evaluation end-to-end: scoping, custom environment setup, POC design, success criteria definition, security review support, and close

Build — Actually Build

  • Build pragmatic API integrations to customer systems, independently or in collaboration with customer engineering teams, and unblock evaluations without needing to escalate to Dust engineering

  • Build and maintain Dust4Dust internal tooling — agents, workflows, and automations that make the SE team operate at a higher level

Navigate Enterprise Complexity

  • Lead security reviews, IT governance discussions, and compliance conversations (GDPR, data sovereignty, SOC2) with CIOs and IT teams — the things that stall deals if no one owns them

  • Articulate Dust’s differentiation in relation to other agentic platforms as well as in contrast to deterministic automation tools (such as Make, Zapier, n8n).

  • Help define the enterprise pilot playbook: repeatable evaluation frameworks, security approval templates, and integration patterns that scale

Raise the Bar Across the Team

  • Act as the primary feedback loop to Product and Engineering — translate technical friction from customer conversations into structured, actionable roadmap input

  • Mentor and onboard more junior SEs; help establish the craft bar the function will be measured against

  • Contribute to the SE knowledge base: technical documentation, reusable demo assets, and integration playbooks

 

Requirements

Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions. Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.

Aptitude

  • Strong hands-on coding ability: you write Python, TypeScript, or Bash, call APIs directly, and have shipped real integrations — with concrete projects to show, not side projects

  • Deep understanding of integration architecture: APIs, webhooks, data connectors, authentication patterns — you can design and explain this to an engineering team independently

  • Fluency in LLM/AI architecture: RAG pipelines, prompt engineering, agent orchestration, data connectors — you can go deep with ML engineers and data teams without needing backup

  • Experience navigating enterprise security reviews: GDPR, data sovereignty, SOC2, IT governance — you understand the questions and know how to answer them

  • Ability to adapt technical depth for any audience — from C-level to DevOps lead — without dumbing down or losing the engineering teams

Attitude

  • Builder mindset: you don't wait for a playbook — you write it, then make sure others can use it

  • Low ego, high standards: you give direct feedback, receive it without defensiveness, and make the engineers and AEs around you sharper

  • Customer-centric at depth: genuine curiosity about how engineering teams are built and operated, not just the business problem on the surface

  • GenAI-native: you use AI tools as a force multiplier in your own workflow — not as a novelty, but as how you work

  • Mentorship instinct: as an L4+, you actively invest in the growth of more junior SEs — through code reviews, deal coaching, and knowledge sharing

Agency

  • Technical self-sufficiency: when you hit a wall, you debug it yourself first — then bring back what you learned to improve how the team operates

  • Proactive infrastructure builder: you see gaps in how the SE team operates and build tools or systems to fix them without being asked

  • End-to-end deal ownership: from the first technical call to security approval and POC close, you own the outcome — not just your stage

  • Roadmap influence: you don't just flag product gaps — you validate them across customers, assess priority, and bring structured proposals to Product and Engineering

  • Scope expansion mindset: you define your role by outcomes, not job description — and consistently find problems to solve that no one assigned you

 

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: £120 - £155k base salary

  • 🏡 We offer substantial support for relocation (up to 10k), including finding an apartment in London and supporting you with the visa procedure

  • Significant equity package in a Sequoia-backed startup

  • Health insurance for you and your dependents

  • New MacBook Pro or Linux machine, monitor, keyboard, etc.

  • Opportunity to travel to the US multiple times a year

  • Regular team events and offsite

We can go higher for outstanding profiles.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Most CFOs inherit a finance function.

This one gets to build it.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer — quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We hold the power of attorney for every customer, take decisions, do the work, and take legal responsibility for the result.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. That means making correct and fair employment simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where we stand

Thousands of clients rely on us. Last year alone, over CHF 200 million ran through our platform. We are at CHF 7 million ARR and growing. The Swiss business is profitable. We have acquired two new businesses in the last twelve months. A hungry team of over 50 people (and 5 dogs) in offices in Switzerland, Germany and the United Kingdom. And we are raising our next round.

We do not have a finance function yet. We have an external accountant, a signed audit, and a CEO and COO who know exactly what they need to run this company — but cannot build it alone.

That is the opening.

Tasks

What you will own

Everything financial:

  • Banking architecture across multiple currencies, countries, and entities. Monthly close that actually closes on time.
  • Compliance in multiple jurisdictions via external partners you recruit and manage.
  • The financial diligence in our roll-up strategy when we acquire — and the structuring of acquisition financing when deals need to be funded.
  • A financial model that investors love to look at. The data room when we raise.

You will report to David (CEO) and work closely with Lad (COO), who owns the P&L and will be your closest counterpart on the operational side. You will present to the board. You will be in the room for every capital allocation decision.

There is no team. There is no process to maintain. There is a blank sheet and a business that is ready to run properly.

The first year

Your first year at quinn is one of the rare opportunities where you get to make every decision that matters. Which tools. Which banks. Which partners. How we report, how we model, how we show up to investors. All of it is yours to design.

You will spend the first months getting under the hood — taking over the books, understanding the gaps, and fixing what needs fixing first. You will build the reporting infrastructure that gives leadership real visibility to steer the company across every product and revenue stream.

You will analyze the first potential merger and acquisition targets and sit in rooms where the financial direction of the company gets decided, and you will be the person with the numbers.

By the end of the year, you will have built something real: a finance function that works, a roll-up strategy that has financial legs, and a leadership team that trusts you completely. Most people at this level spend years waiting for that kind of ownership. Here it happens within months.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

You have been CFO or Head of Finance at a scale-up — a SaaS, marketplace, or tech-enabled services company. You have worked across more than one international market. You are comfortable closing the books yourself, not just reviewing what others produce. You have built financial infrastructure before — not inherited it.

You are equally at home in B2C and B2B — and you understand what it means to manage the unit economics, reporting, and compliance obligations for both within a single business.

You think in MRR, ARR, NRR, CAC payback, and LTV:CAC ratio. You have worked with investors. You understand what a roll-up strategy looks like financially, and you have the accounting basics to back it up. You know the difference between managing a finance function and doing the finance — and you are built for the latter.

Most importantly: You want this. Not a senior finance role at a large company. This one. The blank sheet, the multiple markets, the acquisitions to integrate, the round to prepare, the opportunity. The kind of thing you only get to do once.

The Team

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process, a lot of hierarchy, or a lot of patience for people who need it. We do have a profitable core business, a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action

The CFO is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who looks at this and thinks: Finally!

jobs.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Platform Engineering Teams

Our Platform Engineering team builds and operates the cloud infrastructure, automation, and deployment systems that power Wayve’s software development. Working primarily with Azure, the team creates reliable, scalable, and secure platforms that help engineers develop, test, and release software efficiently. You’ll collaborate with teams across Wayve that are advancing embodied AI and autonomous driving.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll build, maintain, and improve cloud infrastructure across development, testing, and production environments. You’ll automate infrastructure provisioning, support CI/CD pipelines, monitor platform performance, and troubleshoot issues affecting reliability or delivery. You’ll also work closely with engineering teams to understand their needs and continuously improve the developer experience.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Cloud infrastructure and services, primarily within Azure

  • Infrastructure as Code using tools such as Terraform and Ansible

  • Cloud-based CI/CD pipelines and deployment systems

  • Containerised workloads and orchestration platforms

  • Monitoring, observability, security, and cost optimisation

  • Incident response, root-cause analysis, and operational automation

 

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have 2–5 years of experience in DevOps, cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or a related role

  • You have hands-on experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP

  • You’ve worked with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or Ansible

  • You’re familiar with CI/CD systems and cloud-based deployment pipelines

  • You understand networking, cloud architecture, and system reliability fundamentals

  • You’re a collaborative problem-solver who enjoys troubleshooting complex systems and reducing manual work through automation

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

• Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes) — motivation, communication, relevant DevOps and CI/CD experience, Wayve fit, and logistics.

• Competency interview (45 minutes) — hiring manager discussion covering role fit, technical breadth, problem-solving, ownership, and collaboration.

• Deep-dive technical interviews (approximately 3 hours total) — programming, system design, and an SDO domain interview covering build systems, CI/CD infrastructure, automation, Linux, Git, scripting, distributed execution, caching, and artifact management.

• Final interview (60 minutes) — conversation with a director focused on Wayve’s mission and values, operating style, stakeholder communication, and long-term potential.We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

jobs.title: Inside Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place!

We are looking for a high-impact Inside Sales Manager in London to spearhead our high-velocity, sales engine across the UK region. Reporting directly to the Senior Manager, Outbound Sales you will be the strategic architect and frontline leader of our inside sales motion.

You will be responsible for leading a high-performing team of Inside Sales Representatives / and Account Executives (AEs). Your mission is to optimise our digital and phone-based selling motion to generate self-sourced pipeline, execute targeted outbound campaigns, and drive inbound conversion across key UK markets.

What you will be doing:

As the Inside Sales Manager, you are the primary driver of proactive, scalable revenue growth across the UK. This is a fast-paced, high-impact position where you will oversee the entire inside sales funnel—from rapid lead response and discovery through to virtual demos and closing mid-market deals.

Your core responsibilities will include:

  • Leading High-Velocity Inside Sales Teams: Manage, coach, and inspire a focused team of Inside Sales AEs and SDRs operating in a fast-paced, metric-driven virtual environment metric-driven virtual environment, with a strong emphasis on proactive prospecting and ‘hunting’.

  • Vertical-Specific Conversion Strategy: Adapt high-velocity inside sales strategies to engage and convert prospects within the Hospitality sector, ensuring messaging aligns with regional nuances and business priorities across the UK.

  • Outbound Pipeline Generation & Funnel Optimisation: Partner closely with Marketing and RevOps to build high-converting outbound strategies, driving self-sourced pipeline while maintaining rapid speed-to-lead on inbound demand.

  • Forecasting & Revenue Intelligence: Reporting directly to the Senior Manager,, provide rigorous weekly and quarterly forecasts. Leverage revenue intelligence tools (Gong, Salesforce, ChurnZero, Pure Cloud, and internal AI-based tools) to review call recordings, spot deal risks, and deliver real-time coaching at scale.

  • Live Call & Deal Coaching: Join virtual pitches and closing calls as an executive sponsor on key deals, helping your reps maintain momentum, build urgency, and close business efficiently without in-person meetings.

And a little bit of....

  • Contributing as an integral part of the wider team to achieve organisational goals, even if this means undertaking tasks outside the strict scope of your primary role.

What you need to bring:

To be successful in this role, you must demonstrate a strong command of high-velocity SaaS sales methodologies and a proven ability to coach reps to peak performance in a hybrid-selling environment.

What you will need:

  • Proven Leadership: Extensive experience in sales management, specifically having managed or led complex, multi-functional sales teams in a fast-paced B2B SaaS environment, selling to SMEs with a transactional sales cycle .

  • Operational Excellence: Expert proficiency in the modern sales stack (Salesforce, Salesloft/Outreach, LinkedIn Sales Navigator etc.) and a data-first approach to territory management.

  • Commercial Acumen: A strong grasp of SaaS financial metrics (ARR, LTV, CAC) and the ability to translate these into strategic outbound initiatives.

  • Hands-On Coaching Style: A passion for call reviews, live role-playing, and KPI-driven performance management that drives consistent daily execution.

What’s in it for you:

You’ll enjoy:

  • A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work

  • A culture that celebrates performance

  • The chance to make an impact in a team that’s big enough for career growth, but lean enough to make your voice heard

  • Career-defining opportunities

Plus benefits designed to keep you happy, healthy and fulfilled.

  • Flexible paid time off and remote work policies

  • Equity options, because this is your company too

  • Contributions to your pension plan. Your future matters

  • Training opportunities to grow your skills and career

  • Health and wellness credit so you feel your best (£400 per year)

  • Time off to volunteer and give back to your community

  • Interest groups, employee led networks, social committees to sponsored sports teams

  • Enhanced parental leave to support growing families

To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Who we are:

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.

Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

Lightspeed handles your information in accordance with our Applicant Privacy Statement.

jobs.description:
Missions

  • Assurer la coordination administrative du projet RITMEA ;

  • Assurer le pilotage administratif de l’ensemble des activités du consortium en liaison avec le coordinateur scientifique du projet.

Activités principales

  • Assurer le pilotage administratif et le suivi des engagements financiers du projet RITMEA (axe 3) ;

  • Assurer la coordination administrative, y compris financière ;

  • Participer aux réunions du projet ;

  • Rédiger les comptes rendus et relevés de décisions ;

  • Participer à l’instruction de dossiers ;

  • Assister les partenaires sur les aspects administratifs ;

  • Accompagner la gestion du projet avec le référent scientifique en coopération avec les services concernés à l’UTC (direction des affaires financières (DAF) - notamment) et en interaction avec l’équipe administrative du laboratoire ;

  • Assurer le suivi du budget global du projet ;

  • Assurer le suivi des plannings et des indicateurs ;

  • Effectuer les reportings et les bilans avec le référent scientifique du projet ;

  • Participer aux événements de promotion liés au projet ;

  • Suivre la production des publications scientifiques en lien avec le projet.

Le/La chargé(e) de coordination et de gestion de projet de recherche en mobilité éco-responsable et autonome travaille en étroite collaboration avec les interlocuteurs des services supports de l’UTC et les correspondants du consortium dont il est l’interlocuteur privilégié. Il est amené à échanger très régulièrement avec les partenaires du projet et plus généralement avec les différents acteurs concernés par celui-ci.

Il est doté d’une bonne capacité d’adaptation aux différents interlocuteurs et sait faire preuve de professionnalisme dans la communication écrite et orale.

Informations complémentaires

Dates pour candidater

Du 24/11/2026 au 08/01/2027

Type de contrat et dates prévisionnelles de recrutement

Contrat à durée déterminée – pourvoi à partir du 01/01/2027 et jusqu’au 31/12/2027 (prolongation possible)

Salaire mensuel brut

Selon expérience et financement

Volume horaire

37 heures et 30 minutes/semaine – 1 607 heures/an

Congés

50 jours de congés, RTT comprise, par année universitaire

Lieu de travail

Compiègne

Environnement et contexte de travail

Le poste est à pourvoir au département génie informatique au sein du laboratoire Heudiasyc, (UMR CNRS UTC 7253), qui mène des recherches dans le domaine des sciences du numérique, de l’informatique, de la robotique et de l’intelligence artificielle.

L’activité est dédiée au projet RITMEA (Recherche et Innovation en Transports et Mobilités Eco-responsables et Automatisés) axe 3 (Automatisation des véhicules : automobile, ferroviaire, fluvial, drones http://www.frttm.fr/ritmea) financé dans le cadre du contrat de plan État région (CPER), porté administrativement et scientifiquement par le laboratoire Heudiasyc et en gestion conjointe entre Heudiasyc et l’UTC. Le consortium de l’axe 3 comprend 9 partenaires. Le projet est cofinancé par l’Union Européenne, l’Etat et la Région.

La personne recrutée intègre l’équipe administrative et financière du laboratoire, comprenant 6 personnes. Elle rend compte à ses responsables : porteur UTC du projet et responsable administratif.

Des déplacements sont à prévoir dans le cadre du projet pour des réunions professionnelles, et des événements ponctuels dans la région Hauts de France.

Le recrutement s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet CPER RITMEA  (Recherche et Innovation en Transports et Mobilités Eco-responsables et Automatisés), Axe 3 (Automatisation des véhicules : automobile, ferroviaire, fluvial,drones)


Compétences

  • Pilotage des échéances et suivi des livrables ;

  • Connaissances budgétaires, gestion financière ;

  • Aptitude au travail en réseau ;

  • Maîtrise des outils bureautiques et nouveaux médias de travail à distance (plateformes collaboratives, webconférence, zoom, etc.) ;

  • Sens des priorités ;

  • Autonomie et sens du travail en équipe.

Diplôme, formation et habilitation

  • Diplôme : licence au minimum, master apprécié ;

  • Domaines de formation : gestion administrative et sciences de gestion, management de l’innovation et des projets de R&D, affaires européennes et internationales, développement territorial et politiques publiques, administration de la recherche et de l’enseignement supérieur, transition écologique, énergie et mobilités.

Toute formation complétée par une expérience avérée dans le montage et le suivi de projets collaboratifs (régionaux, nationaux ou européens) sera considérée.
